text.brief: On May 23, 1962, John Kennedy told reporters that the United States would admit several thousand refugees who had fled the mainland into Hong Kong.
text.record: Famine and a loosened border sent tens of thousands of people from Guangdong into Hong Kong in April and May 1962, and Hong Kong's government returned most of them ([FRUS 1961-63, Vol. XXV, Document 318: U.S. delegation report to the UNHCR Executive Committee](https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1961-63v25/d318)). Kennedy used the attorney general's parole power to admit refugees outside the quota system. About fifteen thousand arrived over the next three years.
text.reading: The parole answered a famine the Party would not admit with a door the quota law would not open. The executive shielded people by decision because the statute had no rule for them.
text.gapText: Architecture Principles. The quota system had no category for people fleeing a famine their government denied.
text.fix: Keep a standing refugee authority with published criteria, so rescue does not depend on a press conference.
